subject: general
question: ________ convention proposes that while accounting for various transactions, only those which may have significant effect on profitability or financial status of the business should have special consideration for reporting.
solution:
The correct answer is** Materiality.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Materiality convention proposes that while accounting for various transactions, only those which may have significant effect on profitability or financial status of the business should have special consideration for reporting:**

 
 
• The materiality principle in accounting suggests that all significant information that could influence the decision of a user of financial statements should be disclosed.
 
• Transactions or items are considered material if their omission or misstatement could influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of the financial statements.
 
• This principle helps in focusing on the most relevant and impactful financial information, ensuring that users get a clear and accurate picture of the business's financial status.
 
• Materiality is subjective and may vary depending on the size and nature of the business and the specific circumstances of the transaction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Consistency:**

 
 
• This principle states that companies should use the same accounting methods and procedures from period to period unless a change is justified and disclosed. It ensures comparability of financial statements over different periods but does not relate to the significance of transactions.
 
 
 
• **Historical cost:**
 
 
• This principle requires assets to be recorded at their original purchase cost. It does not consider the significance of transactions in terms of their effect on profitability or financial status.
 
 
 
• **Conservatism:**
 
 
• This principle advises that potential expenses and liabilities should be recognized as soon as possible, but revenue should only be recognized when it is assured. While it impacts the reporting of financial status, it does not specifically address the materiality of transactions.
